name: Name
body: Battle Forge is a monthly series that presents a new WARMACHINE scenario in each installment. Battle Forge scenarios emphasize the narrative unfolding over the course of a game and may be asymmetrical, uneven, and even somewhat experimental because the goal of Battle Forge is to create a sandbox toolset that allows for creative scenario generation and new, story-worthy experiences with WARMACHINE! Players are encouraged to modify Battle Forge scenarios in any way that makes the scenario more appropriate for their army collections and their available terrain resources. Most important of all, have fun! And if you find a better way to do something with a scenario that results in a better experience for you, let us know at feedback@privateerpress.com, so we can try it, too!

name: Name
body: Following are the key terms that will be repeated in many Battle Forge scenarios:

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models, uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective, uncontested.

name: Name
body: Battle Forge victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set amount of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body: In addition to its standard rules, each Battle Forge scenario has two random tables that add additional Victory Point-scoring opportunities for players that vary each time the scenario is played. Mission Modifiers add additional scoring opportunities based on the position of a player’s models on the table. Achievements add additional scoring opportunities based on a player’s actions taken on the battlefield. Players should roll a d6 to randomly determine Mission Modifiers and Achievements before the beginning of a game, or players can choose them at will if all players agree. It is recommended that only one Mission Modifier and one Achievement should be in effect during any match (unless you really want to get crazy).

name: Name
body: If a player makes an attack that destroys one or more friendly models, that player’s opponent gains 1 Victory Point. If a player makes an attack and destroys their own Leader model, that player immediately loses the match.

name: Name
body: In addition to objectives, Battle Forge scenarios will routinely draw on the following terrain elements. Dimensions provided are approximations, and you should feel free to substitute any terrain pieces you have available as necessary. Use the resources you have available to get close enough to maintain the spirit and intention of the scenario.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 3/4" x 4". Barriers provide cover.

name: Name
body: Obstructions with an approximate footprint of 5" x 5".

name: Name
body: Forest areas with an approximate footprint of 5" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 2" × 2". Small obstacles provide cover.

name: Name
body: An elevated platform at least 1" above the table, such as a hill or terrace. Plateaus can possess multiple areas at different heights that models can be placed on, but the areas must be level to prevent models from falling over. If a model cannot be placed on a level area without risk of falling off, it cannot occupy that area. Models cannot be placed on slopes, and we recommend that plateau terrain with sloped surfaces not be used. Hill, Small—A plateau platform with a footprint approximately 6" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 30 mm models to be placed on. Hill, Large—A plateau with a footprint approximately 6" to 12" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 40 mm models to be placed on.

name: Name
body: An area of shallow water approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An area of rubble approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: A 3" × 5" trench template.

name: Name
body: If there was a method to his madness, surely Zacchaeus was the only one who understood it. What was known for certain was that the shifty Grymkin also known as The Winter’s Chill had stealthily stolen a satchel stuffed with secrets snatched from both invaders and defenders alike. They were the kind of secrets that could tip the balance of a war that was already on uneven footing. They were the kind of secrets worth dying for—so long as one was content chasing a giant rabbit at their peril.

name: Name
body: "MARCH HARE" is designed to be played with 30- or 50-point forces.

name: Name
body: "MARCH HARE" ends after five rounds.

name: Name
body: Zacchaeus, the Winter’s Chill, has stolen valuable military intelligence that all sides have deemed worth recovering at any cost. As he races chaotically around the battlefield, players compete to intercept Zacchaeus in an effort to force the Grymkin to drop the intel so they can snatch it up. But while Zacchaeus moves at random, each player can activate him once during each of their turns in order to use his Combat Action. The player who recovers the most intel before the end of the match will win the day.

name: Name
body: Recover as many Stolen Intel objectives from Zacchaeus as possible.

name: Name
body: This scenario requires Zacchaeus, the Winter’s Chill. Begin setup by placing Zacchaeus in the center of the map. This scenario does not use a predesigned map. Instead, players should take turns placing whatever terrain they have available.

name: Name
body:
This scenario uses Execution Mode.
March Hare—During each player’s Maintenance Phase, Zacchaeus must be moved d6+3" in a random direction.  During this movement, Zacchaeus advances through any intervening models with an equal or smaller base size if he has enough movement to move entirely past the model’s base. If Zacchaeus contacts an obstruction or a model with a larger base size, randomly determine a new trajectory for the remainder of his movement.
If on any turn Zacchaeus is prevented from moving at least 6" due to terrain or intervening models, immediately place Zacchaeus at his starting point at the center of the map and move him d6+3" in a random direction.
During each player’s Activation Phase, that player can make one Combat Action using Zacchaeus and can then use his Reposition special rule.
Zacchaeus is never considered to be a friendly model.
Once per turn, the first time a player damages Zacchaeus with an attack, their opponent must place a 20 mm Stolen Intel objective within 1" of Zaccheus.

name: Name
body:
If a player boxes Zacchaeus, instead of being destroyed, he becomes knocked down instead. If a player ends their turn with their Leader models within 1" of Zacchaeus while he is knocked down, they gain 3 Victory Points. At the start of the next player’s turn, remove all damage from Zacchaeus. If Zacchaeus is knocked down, Zacchaeus is no longer knocked down.
Players can recover any Stolen Intel objectives secured by warrior models at the end of their turn. For each recovered objective, that player gains 1 Victory Point.

name: Name
body: Roll once on both the Mission Modifiers and Achievement tables.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Mission Modifier for this match: 1. Have Some Wine—Each time a player damages Zacchaeus, their Leader suffers d3 damage. 2. Harebrained—If Zacchaeus is within 5" of any or both Leader models during a player’s Maintenance Phase, instead of randomizing his movement, move him directly toward the closest Leader. 3. Queen of Hearts—Attacks made by Zacchaeus targeting Leader or Cohort models get boosted attack and damage rolls.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Achievement for this match. 1. Get What You Like—The first player to damage Zacchaeus gains 1 Victory Point. 2. Like What You Get—The first player with a model destroyed by an attack made by Zacchaeus gains 1 Victory Point. 3. Lucky Rabbit’s Foot—The first player to end their turn with at least three warrior models within 1" of Zacchaeus gains 2 Victory Points.

name: Name
body: Victory conditions are checked in the following order: Decisive Win: At the end of five rounds, the player with the most Stolen Intel wins. Point Advantage Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, if a player has 7 or more Victory Points than their opponent, they win the match. Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match. Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match.
